facts.text: HamiltonInterface is the main class that sets up and tears down the interface to a Hamilton robot and creates a Hamilton HSL background process plus a localhost connection
start() launches the pyhamilton interpreter/OEM application and the local HTTP server, and is_open() returns the active flag
stop() terminates the OEM process in normal mode, sets active to False and joins the server thread with a 1.0 s timeout

start() opens the OEM application with a window for simulation, only sets active in simulating mode, starts a 32-bit server process in server mode, and otherwise starts a new OEM process (run_hamilton_process)
is_open() returns True between start() and stop()
initialize() sends the INITIALIZE command and waits up to 300 s for its response
aspirate() refuses a command without a liquidClass and accepts at most 8 positions
dispense() accepts at most 8 positions and uses the upstream default liquid class when none is given
aspirate() and dispense() return AspirateResult or DispenseResult with liquidHeights and liquidVolumes
move_by_seq() sends ISWAP_GET for the source sequence and ISWAP_PLACE for the target sequence, each with a 120 s response timeout
set_labware_property() sends SET_LABWARE_PROPERTY with LabwareID, PropertyName and PropertyValue
HamiltonServerThread.has_exited reports whether the local server thread has left its run loop
The usable pipetting volume is derived from the installed tip type and the liquid class, not from a fixed robot bound
The project is developed for Hamilton STAR and STARlet on Windows; VANTAGE is supported with a plugin
The clone's tests mock HamiltonInterface.start and HamiltonInterface.stop; it ships no device simulator for these actions
The simulating flag only logs commands and returns no response data instead of emulating the robot
